Note-stream command jump table @2d85 (dispatched via `rst #20` after `and #0f` at 2d82-2d84 on a stream byte >= #f0). 16 little-endian word entries: #f0->2f55 (jump), #f1->2f65 (waveform), #f2->2f77 (octave shift), #f3->2f89 (volume), #f4->2f9b (volume-effect), #f5-#fe->000c (a bare ret, unused), #ff->2fad (end). Cites the first entry byte 55 @2d85 (the table is data the disassembler renders as code); entries continue through 2da4 (`ad 2f`, line 6332-6333).

Command #f0 handler @2f55: reads the 2-byte little-endian operand at the note pointer (ix+6/7) and REPLACES the note pointer with it — an absolute jump/loop within the stream (the looping intermission streams end with `f0 fb 3b` / `f0 9d 3c`). The start-theme streams never use it; they end with #ff.

Command #f1 handler @2f65: one operand byte -> ix+3, the voice WAVEFORM select. The interrupt driver routes it to the WSG hardware waveform register while a note-stream is active (pacman.asm:00ac-00b4 reads #4ecf = tune-struct ix+3 when #4ecc is nonzero). Start theme: bass f1 02 (waveform 2), melody f1 00 (waveform 0).

Command #f2 handler @2f77: one operand byte -> ix+4, the BASE FREQUENCY SHIFT. At note output (2de5) the shift count = ix+4 plus the note byte bit4, and the 16-bit word = pitch-table byte << shift (2ee4-2ee7 `add hl,hl` loop). Start theme: bass f2 03, melody f2 02.
Command #f3 handler @2f89: one operand byte -> ix+9, the 4-bit VOLUME latched into ix+0f at each note start (2dad-2db9). Both start-theme streams use f3 0f (full volume).

Command #f4 handler @2f9b: one operand byte -> ix+0b, the VOLUME-EFFECT select dispatched per frame via `rst #20` through the table @2f02 (2efe-2f01): 0 -> 2f22 (flat: return ix+0f), 1 -> 2f26 (decay: decrement ix+0f once per frame toward 0), 2/3/4 -> slower decays gated on the frame counter #4c84. Start theme: bass f4 01 (the plucked decay), melody f4 00 (flat).

Volume-effect 1 handler @2f26 (reached from the @2f02 dispatch): reads ix+0f and falls into 2f34 `and #0f; ret z; dec a; ld (ix+#0f),a` — the running note volume decrements by 1 each engine frame until 0. This is the start-theme bass PLUCK envelope (bass stream sets f4 01).

Command #ff handler @2fad: clears this sound request bit out of ix+0 (`cpl / and (ix+#00)`) and jumps to the silence path 2df4 (zeroes the voice frequency/volume registers). End of a finite tune — both start-theme streams terminate with #ff (bass @3bf2, melody @3c94).

meaning: Note handler @2da5 (stream bytes < #f0): the note byte b is split — top 3 bits (rlca x3, `and #07` @2dbc-2dc0) index the duration table #3bb0 (frames = 1<<idx) into the counter ix+0c; low 4 bits (`and #0f` @2dce) index the pitch table #3bb8 into ix+0e; low 5 bits == 0 (`and #1f` z @2dca) sustains the previous pitch for the duration; pitch idx 0 with bit4 set (e.g. #50/#70) is a REST (table byte 00 -> frequency 0).

Note output @2ddc-2de5: bit4 of the stored note byte (ix+0d `and #10`) adds 1 to the shift count on top of the base shift ix+4 (`add a,(ix+#04)` @2de5) — a per-note +1 octave. The 16-bit word (pitch byte << shift) is then written as 4 nibbles into the voice frequency registers @2ee8-2efb; voice 1 registers are frequency bits 0-15 (5-nibble voice), voices 2/3 registers are bits 4-19, an implicit further x16.
